I overweighted accidental deletion. The specific case is a writable mount turning an ordinary rm or mv into B2 operations. B2 has no atomic file rename, so moves can become copy then delete; the current log: config also has hard_delete=true, which permanently removes files on deletion instead of retaining a hidden version. That is a recovery hazard, but a read-only mount would obstruct the file organization you expect. A bucket-scoped key that permits normal moves, hard_delete=false, a sensible version-retention policy, and a separately tested backup are better controls if a writable mount proves useful. rclone move, rclone B2 versions and hard delete, Backblaze file versions

The 1Password names now reflect the two roles. Backblaze administration retains the existing account-wide key and its local .env mount. logseq-encode-publishing exists but has no variables or mount yet. The current rclone wrapper still reads the old mount path, so the two roles are not operationally separated until a bucket-scoped key is created and the wrapper is switched.

The concern about a read-only mount is fair. The real requirement is that an agent can author a public page from another checkout without this Mac's mount. A stable URL on a media domain you control lets Logseq, GitHub, CI, and remote agents read an existing public asset directly. A local mount or downloaded copy can remain an optional editing convenience. For newly created remote assets, an agent needs a scoped upload path; otherwise the page should use an existing URL or an asset committed to Git until upload is available. This is a design proposal, pending the choice between source URLs and relative links above.

rclone mount presents B2 as a filesystem, but a remote file read may fetch data on a cache miss, and directory access may require remote listing. The number of B2 requests depends on rclone's VFS and directory caches; a filesystem read is not always one B2 request. At current Backblaze pay-as-you-go pricing, Class A/B/C API calls are free, while direct downloads count against the included egress of 3× average monthly storage before overage charges. The larger practical costs for this workflow may be latency, offline failure, and sandbox access to FUSE or credentials. Measure a small mount pilot before depending on it. rclone mount and VFS cache, Backblaze transaction pricing, Backblaze B2 pricing

Use assets/.remote/ for named local working files and the .dvc files that describe them. Git stores the .dvc metadata; DVC restores selected working files from B2. Public episode URLs refer to separately uploaded files with page-derived names.
The September 24 MP3 is registered with DVC and restores from B2 into a fresh checkout. Adding the asset tasks and conversion pipeline are the next actions under Put the layout to work.
The September 24 MP3 uses this layout:

dvc add assets/.remote/GitP___A___Session___26___09___24-Thu___Asset___Synth___Full.mp3 creates the adjacent .mp3.dvc file. Inside that metadata, path: GitP___A___Session___26___09___24-Thu___Asset___Synth___Full.mp3 means the MP3 beside the .dvc file. DVC's file format defines paths relative to the metadata file's directory.

A fresh clone contains assets/.remote/GitP___A___Session___26___09___24-Thu___Asset___Synth___Full.mp3.dvc. Running dvc pull assets/.remote/GitP___A___Session___26___09___24-Thu___Asset___Synth___Full.mp3.dvc restores assets/.remote/GitP___A___Session___26___09___24-Thu___Asset___Synth___Full.mp3. Running dvc pull restores all assets described by the checkout's DVC metadata. DVC pull targets explains selecting one asset.

Commit the adjacent .dvc files and .dvc/config. DVC's generated .dvc/.gitignore excludes its local cache and runtime files. Pipeline definitions and their result checksums belong in dvc.yaml and dvc.lock when a conversion pipeline is added.
The garden's ignore rules allow DVC metadata anywhere beneath assets/.remote/ while excluding the working files:

The directory exception lets Git reach nested metadata. The .dvc exception makes the metadata eligible for commit. git add assets/.remote/GitP___A___Session___26___09___24-Thu___Asset___Synth___Full.mp3.dvc stages the metadata; the MP3 remains ignored.

Configure the DVC remote as s3://logseq-encode-garden/dvc/ with endpoint https://s3.us-east-005.backblazeb2.com. DVC stores file content beneath that prefix using checksum-derived names such as dvc/files/md5/<first-two-characters>/<remaining-characters>.

DVC reads the checksum in the .dvc file to find the B2 object, downloads it to its local .dvc/cache/, and restores the named file under assets/.remote/. The local path and B2 object name serve different purposes: the local path identifies the recording; the storage name identifies its contents.

assets/.remote/ contains the files selected for the current checkout. DVC can list and retrieve files represented by that checkout's metadata. Browsing arbitrary existing B2 objects requires the B2 client; those objects gain DVC tracking only when explicitly added or imported.
GitP/A/Log/26/10/04 Sun/Fnox/Plan supplies the garden's B2 credentials from the encrypted cache on the Mac. DVC's compatible-server settings describes using a Backblaze endpoint with the S3 client.
